about: Substrate dashboard cookbook — copyable surface recipes. Each recipe is a folder of plain markdown files: the dashboard note plus every sheet, database note, or contact it binds to, so a copied recipe renders with numbers on the first open. Install = copy the recipe's files into your vault (keep the Dashboards/ nesting or don't — folders never decide database membership). An agent can read any recipe and adapt the sample rows, formulas, and card binds to your real data.

recipes.title: Portfolio
recipes.blurb: Stat cards over a sheet. The sheet holds rows and formulas; the dashboard binds cards to the named summaries — total, per-bucket sums — and every number traces back to the file.
recipes.adapt: Replace the csv rows in Holdings.md with your positions; add summaries in the formulas fence and bind more cards to them.

recipes.title: Food log
recipes.blurb: A daily net-kcal tracker with a goal band. Rows live in a log sheet the pane appends to; negative kcal is exercise. A second sheet holds stable kcal bases the autocomplete prices from.
recipes.adapt: Set floor/ceiling to your band, clear the sample log rows, and grow Food DB.md with the foods you actually eat.

recipes.title: News feed
recipes.blurb: A curated newsfeed an external agent writes — one sheet of ranked items with a blurb and a personal why per row. The app writes exactly one column back: your up/down verdicts, which the curator reads before the next sweep.
recipes.adapt: Point an agent at News Items.md with your topics and taste; the fb column is its feedback loop.

recipes.title: Home hub
recipes.blurb: A designed home page from ordinary markdown: headings become section labels, runs of callouts become side-by-side cards for now / deadlines / later, and live cards and chart fences put a sheet's figures in the middle of the page — with wikilinks jumping straight to the notes they name.
recipes.adapt: Rewrite the callouts as your actual now/next, rebind the cards and chart to your own sheet's summaries, and retarget the recipe's view fences and sample releases at your own types.

recipes.title: Release charts
recipes.blurb: Bar charts over a database and a sheet — one chart fence each. x buckets a property (with day/week/month date bucketing), y counts, sums, or averages; a malformed fence renders its error in place and never breaks the others.
recipes.adapt: Change source: to any of your types or {{sheets}}; add fences for more charts.

recipes.title: Label accounting
recipes.blurb: A workbook: overview cards over a statements sheet, with the statement lines, the artist-split ledger, and the release database each one tab away on the strip at the bottom.
recipes.adapt: Replace the statement and split rows with your own; the owed/net summaries recompute, and the pages list in the dashboard's frontmatter is yours to extend.

recipes.title: Finance hub
recipes.blurb: A full personal-finance workbook: net worth over your accounts, budgets against what you actually spent, who-owes-whom in either direction, and a ten-year forecast — four boards and eight sheets on one tab strip. Five sheets are yours to type in; the three machine sheets are regenerated by one small scheduled script, because a compounding curve, a twelve-month projection and a median are exactly what a formula language without row generation cannot express. The workbook note carries the setup: what the daily job does, the launchd plist and the cron one-liner, and the read/write contract to hand an agent.
recipes.adapt: Put your own accounts, fixed costs, budget limits and debts in the five hand-edited sheets and everything above recomputes. Then make it recurring, per the workbook note's "Making it recurring" section: one daily script fetches prices into Accounts, recomputes Budget Limits' spent column from your real spending, and regenerates Forecast Cashflow, Forecast Net Worth and Upcoming whole, stamping each with the time it ran. Schedule it with the launchd plist (bootstrap into gui/$(id -u), log to ~/Library/Logs) or the cron line for Linux — or hand the note to your agent with "write refresh.py against these files and schedule it daily", since the bullet contract there names every file it reads, the two it may touch a single column of, and the three it owns outright. Each run stamps `exported:` on the three sheets it regenerates, so the workbook carries the age of its own numbers and a job that quietly stops is readable from the sheets.

recipes.title: Work index
recipes.blurb: Years of production work, pivoted. A scanner script or agent writes one sheet row per job; the board reads it and answers what the folder tree can't — by year, by client, by category. The app never writes back.
recipes.adapt: Write your own scanner for whatever tree you keep work in — one csv row per job is the whole contract.

recipes.title: Annual report
recipes.blurb: The year, as the vault saw it: headline cards over an annual stats sheet, monthly charts underneath. An agent writes the sheet once a year from version history — every edit is already a snapshot — and the head's Print action turns the pane into the shareable PDF.
recipes.adapt: Have an agent fill Vault 2025.md from your history (notes created, words added, rows grown per month), or hand-edit the rows; add cards and chart fences for whatever else you track.

recipes.title: Studio year
recipes.blurb: Two year grids over one log sheet — one square per day, shaded by how long you sat down, then by how often. The year comes from the rows, not from a setting, so the grid keeps telling the truth as the log grows.
recipes.adapt: Log your own sessions in Studio Log.md — a date column and a number column is the whole contract; point date: and value: at them (value: count needs no number at all).

recipes.title: Release arc
recipes.blurb: Every release as a bar from the day recording started to the day it shipped, lanes grouped by status; a release with no end date is a dot rather than a bar, so nothing is claimed about when it lands. A second fence narrows the same data to what actually shipped.
recipes.adapt: Give your own type two date props (here recording_start and released) and point start:/end: at them; group: buckets the lanes and query: filters the fence.

recipes.title: Tax readiness
recipes.blurb: Is the tax year fit to hand over? A hub page over two sheets: a cards fence bound to your own aggregate summaries, and a checklist of the receipts still owed. Plain fences, no kind of its own — whatever keeps your books stays canonical, and the head's Print action is the page you hand to whoever files.
recipes.adapt: Rename the categories and summaries in the aggregates sheet to whatever your filing is judged on and repoint the cards fence at them (at most two emph: true), then rewrite the Still owed checklist whenever the books re-export the missing-evidence snapshot.

recipes.title: Working task board
recipes.blurb: Every open `type: task` note as one board, late work first: overdue, due today, then a section per area — and a task you pick for today lifts into its own Today section ahead of the groups. Inside a section the order is due bucket, then priority, then age, so rot is the tiebreaker rather than the headline. Rows check off and edit in place, done work drops off, and a snoozed task falls into its own collapsed section instead of vanishing.
recipes.adapt: List under areas: the areas you want sections for — leave it out and every area gets one — and set stale_days: to the age at which an untouched row should start showing its rot. The tasks are ordinary notes: type: task and status:, plus any of due:, priority:, area:, today: with a date to pick one for that day, or snoozed_until: to put one down for a while.

recipes.title: Release weeks (a kind you own)
recipes.blurb: Not a built-in: the renderer ships inside the recipe, at .vault/kinds/week-numbers/. The year draws as ISO weeks shaded by how many releases landed in each one, this week outlined, each square opening its first note (the rest listed in its tooltip). It is one plain ES module written against the documented kind API (vault-format.md §5.8) — the custom-kind path walked from the docs alone.
recipes.adapt: The board's own props drive it: track: is the type: to count, date: the date property to bucket on, year: the year to draw. To make it yours, edit .vault/kinds/week-numbers/index.js — it is a plain file in your vault, not something the app owns (drop docs/kind-api.d.ts beside it and the @type annotation types it in any editor). Substrate asks you to enable the bundle once, and asks again whenever its bytes change, so an edit costs one more confirmation. Install this recipe once per vault: a second install lands copies beside the bundle files rather than replacing them, and the folder's shape is what the app reads.
